extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and war correspondents (journalists)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and dispatching frontline news about Korean War battles, military communiqués, and press–military relations; includes expectations about discretion, accuracy, and cooperation with military authorities. Focuses on wartime journalism practices and handling of sensitive operational information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound reporting depends on reporters' judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sound reporting rested on the almost intuitive judgment of trained newspapermen."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MacArthur said the Army could not provide a list of regulations to be observed in war reporting; proper coverage depended upon individual judgment. Reporters are expected to use their professional judgment when selecting and framing war news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not disclose information valuable to the enemy ('aid and comfort')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army objected that the correspondents were "guilty of disclosing information that would be of value to the enemy and would have a bad morale and psychological effect on our own troops."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing operational details or statements that could assist enemy forces or harm troop morale. This is cited as grounds for denying correspondents re-entry or punitive action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise discretion and cooperate with military authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondents were denied re-entry for "continued failure to observe discretion or cooperation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists in the war zone should exercise discretion about sensitive material and, where appropriate, cooperate with military guidance to avoid compromising operations or morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not engage in false reporting or suppress pertinent facts
rubrics_metrics.description: MacArthur said he was "not advocating false reporting nor the suppression of pertinent facts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain factual accuracy and avoid deliberate suppression of important information; balance transparency with operational security concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensationalism and reporting that 'makes the army look bad'
rubrics_metrics.description: Army claimed some dispatches were "sensational" and "made the army look bad."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from sensationalized language or framing that overstates or dramatizes events in a way that misrepresents military actions or unduly harms institutions; aim for measured, evidence-based reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider psychological/morale impact when selecting and framing stories
rubrics_metrics.description: MacArthur noted that the "psychological factor was an important part of [a] military campaign" and urged correspondents to exercise judgment in news selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should be mindful of the potential morale and psychological effects of their reporting on troops and the public, seeking a balanced 'leavening' in coverage when circumstances warrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use security‑conversant officers to advise correspondents (proposed practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suggestion was made that "officers conversant with security be assigned to work with correspondents" so reporters could be guided and advised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When feasible, embed or consult security‑aware military officers to review or advise on potentially sensitive reporting to avoid unintended operational disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide regular briefings to correspondents for better reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Bureau chiefs requested "regular briefings of correspondents stationed in Tokyo so that the leavening reporting... could be presented."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold consistent, timely briefings to supply reporters with authoritative information and context, enabling more accurate, balanced, and less speculative coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and follow a correspondents' code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: One correspondent said, "I helped to frame in Korea a correspondents code on ... issues" and asserted adherence to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and follow an internal code (ethical/security guidelines) for war correspondents to guide decisions about what to report and how to report sensitive material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise care and safety on the front
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer cautioned correspondents "to be careful on the front, noting two correspondents already have been lost."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should prioritize personal safety and situational awareness when operating in combat zones and follow military safety guidance where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive for factual, objective reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Defending correspondent: "The stories I wrote ... were in the best United Press tradition --- factual and objective as I saw the situation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain objectivity and factual accuracy in dispatches; ground claims in observable evidence and first‑hand reporting to withstand scrutiny and counter accusations of bias or sensationalism.
